newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Auctions of Southeast Asian art rack up $6.7 mln.
newsitem.headline: Auctions of Southeast Asian art rack up $6.7 mln.

text.p: British auction houses Sotheby's and Christie's racked up sales of about S$9.4 million (US$6.7 million) in two separate auctions of Southeast Asian paintings and rare wines at the weekend, the two houses said on Monday.
Sotheby's had sales of S$3.8 million while Christie's sales reached S$5.6 million.

The top-seller at Christie's on Sunday was a painting by Walter Spies, "View Across the Sawahs to Gunung Agung", which sold for just over one million Singapore dollars against its original estimate of S$500,000-S$700,000.
Four paintings by Adrien Jean Le Mayeur de Merpres, a Belgian who settled in Bali, Indonesia, in 1932, were sold by Christie's for a total of S$671,500.
Another of the artist's paintings sold at the Sotheby's auction on Saturday for S$333,750.
More than 400 people participated in the auctions, with several collectors phoning in their bids.
"We are very pleased with today's results which clearly show that the market for Southeast Asian art is strong and well-supported by a broad base of serious collectors," a Sotheby's statement said.

Philip Ng, managing director of Christie's Asia, said in a statement the auction house hopes to introduce new choices for collectors in its next auctions of Southeast Asian art in Singapore in March, 1997.
Another Christie's official said this may include some Vietnamese paintings.
